correctness.rationale: The geometric fixed locus of the swap on the antichain complex of [n]×[n] has orbit-barycenter vertices of two types: diagonal d_i and off-diagonal pair p_{ij}. Re-deriving compatibility by testing every cross-orbit coordinate pair gives strict nesting of pair intervals, with at most one internal diagonal singleton. This produces f_{r-1}=C(n,2r−1)+C(n,2r) and 2^n−1 nonempty faces, and four isolated orbit vertices plus one connected component for n>=3. Binomial alternating sum gives the Euler identity. I independently built the full orbit-compatibility graph and every simplex for each n=3..8 and computed exact integral Smith forms (all nonzero invariants units), with ranks for n8 ∂1=31, ∂2=67, ∂3=9, face vector (36,126,84,9); hence reduced integral H0=Z4,H1=Z28,H2=Z8 and no higher homology. Earlier n=3..7 have H2=0, smaller n cannot have 2-cycles. This is a first-cutoff proof only, not a classification of future n.
